verses.zh: 「你们不可做甚么虚无的神像，不可立雕刻的偶像或是柱像，也不可在你们的地上安甚么錾成的石像，向它跪拜，因为我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: “‘You must not make for yourselves idols,[NOTE:1] so you must not set up for yourselves a carved image or a pillar, and you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down before[NOTE:2] it, for I am the Lord your God.
notes: For the literature regarding the difficult etymology and meaning of the term for “idols” (אֱלִילִם, ʾelilim), see the literature cited in the note on Lev 19:4. It appears to be a diminutive play on words with אֵל (ʾel, “god, God”) and, perhaps at the same time, recalls a common Semitic word for “worthless, weak, powerless, nothingness.” Snaith suggests a rendering of “worthless godlings.”
Heb “on.” The “sculpted stone” appears to be some sort of stone with images carved into (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 181, and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 449).

verses.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must keep my Sabbaths and reverence[NOTE:1] my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “and my sanctuary you shall fear.” Cf. NCV “respect”; CEV “honor.”

verses.zh: 「你们若遵行我的律例，谨守我的诫命，
verses.en: “‘If you walk in my statutes and are sure to obey my commandments,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and my commandments you shall keep and do them.” This appears to be a kind of verbal hendiadys, where the first verb is a modifier of the action of the second verb (see GKC 386 §120.d, although שָׁמַר [shamar, “to keep”] is not cited there; cf. Lev 20:8; 25:18, etc.).

verses.zh: 我就给你们降下时雨，叫地生出土产，田野的树木结果子。
verses.en: I will give you your rains in their time so that[NOTE:1] the land will give its yield and the trees of the field will produce their fruit.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
Heb “the tree of the field will give its fruit.” As a collective singular this has been translated as plural.

verses.zh: 你们打粮食要打到摘葡萄的时候，摘葡萄要摘到撒种的时候；并且要吃得饱足，在你们的地上安然居住。
verses.en: Threshing season will extend for you until the season for harvesting grapes,[NOTE:1] and the season for harvesting grapes will extend until sowing season, so[NOTE:2] you will eat your bread until you are satisfied,[NOTE:3] and you will live securely in your land.
notes: Heb “will reach for you the vintage season.”
Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
Heb “to satisfaction”; KJV, ASV, NASB “to the full.”

verses.zh: 我要赐平安在你们的地上；你们躺卧，无人惊吓。我要叫恶兽从你们的地上息灭；刀剑也必不经过你们的地。
verses.en: I will grant peace in the land so that[NOTE:1] you will lie down to sleep without anyone terrifying you.[NOTE:2] I will remove harmful animals[NOTE:3] from the land, and no sword of war[NOTE:4] will pass through your land.
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
Heb “and there will be no one who terrifies.” The words “to sleep” have been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “harmful animal,” singular, but taken here as a collective plural (so almost all English versions).
Heb “no sword”; the words “of war” are supplied in the translation to indicate what the metaphor of the sword represents.

verses.zh: 你们要追赶仇敌，他们必倒在你们刀下。
verses.en: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to the sword.”

verses.zh: 你们五个人要追赶一百人，一百人要追赶一万人；仇敌必倒在你们刀下。
verses.en: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.

verses.zh: 我要眷顾你们，使你们生养众多，也要与你们坚定所立的约。
verses.en: I will turn to you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and maintain[NOTE:1] my covenant with you.
notes: Heb “cause to arise,” but probably used here for the Lord’s intention of confirming or maintaining the covenant commitment made at Sinai. Cf. KJV “establish”; NASB “will confirm”; NAB “carry out”; NIV “will keep.”

verses.zh: 你们要吃陈粮，又因新粮挪开陈粮。
verses.en: You will still be eating stored produce from the previous year[NOTE:1] and will have to clean out what is stored from the previous year to make room for new.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “old [produce] growing old.”
Heb “and old from the presence of new you will bring out.”

verses.zh: 我要在你们中间立我的帐幕；我的心也不厌恶你们。
verses.en: “‘I will put my tabernacle[NOTE:1] in your midst, and I will not abhor you.[NOTE:2]
notes: LXX codexes Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have “my covenant” rather than “my tabernacle.” Cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV “my dwelling.”
Heb “and my soul [נֶפֶשׁ, nefesh] will not abhor you.”

verses.zh: 我要在你们中间行走；我要作你们的　神，你们要作我的子民。
verses.en: I will walk among you, and I will be your God, and you will be my people.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的　神，曾将你们从埃及地领出来，使你们不作埃及人的奴仆；我也折断你们所负的轭，叫你们挺身而走。」
verses.en: I am the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from being their slaves,[NOTE:1] and I broke the bars of your yoke and caused you to walk upright.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from being to them slaves.”
In other words, to walk as free people and not as slaves. Cf. NIV “with (+ your CEV, NLT) heads held high”; NCV “proudly.”

verses.zh: 「你们若不听从我，不遵行我的诫命，
verses.en: “‘If, however,[NOTE:1] you do not obey me and keep[NOTE:2] all these commandments—
notes: Heb “And if.”
Heb “and do not do.”

verses.zh: 厌弃我的律例，厌恶我的典章，不遵行我一切的诫命，背弃我的约，
verses.en: if you reject my statutes and abhor my regulations so that you do not keep[NOTE:1] all my commandments and you break my covenant—
notes: Heb “to not do.”

verses.zh: 我待你们就要这样：我必命定惊惶，叫眼目干瘪、精神消耗的痨病热病辖制你们。你们也要白白地撒种，因为仇敌要吃你们所种的。
verses.en: I for my part[NOTE:1] will do this to you: I will inflict horror on you, consumption and fever, which diminish eyesight and drain away the vitality of life.[NOTE:2] You will sow your seed in vain because[NOTE:3] your enemies will eat it.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “I also” (see HALOT 76 s.v. אַף 6.b).

Heb “soul.” These expressions may refer either to the physical effects of consumption and fever as the rendering in the text suggests (e.g., J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 452, 454, “diminishing eyesight and loss of appetite”), or perhaps the more psychological effects, “which exhausts the eyes” because of anxious hope “and causes depression” (Heb “causes soul [נֶפֶשׁ, nefesh] to pine away”), e.g., B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 185.
Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have causal force here.
That is, “your enemies will eat” the produce that grows from the sown seed.

verses.zh: 我要向你们变脸，你们就要败在仇敌面前。恨恶你们的，必辖管你们；无人追赶，你们却要逃跑。
verses.en: I will set my face against you. You will be struck down before your enemies; those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when there is no one pursuing you.

verses.zh: 你们因这些事若还不听从我，我就要为你们的罪加七倍惩罚你们。
verses.en: “‘If, in spite of all these things,[NOTE:1] you do not obey me, I will discipline you seven times more on account of your sins.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And if until these.”
Heb “I will add to discipline you seven [times] on your sins.”

verses.zh: 我必断绝你们因势力而有的骄傲，又要使覆你们的天如铁，载你们的地如铜。
verses.en: I will break your strong pride and make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.

verses.zh: 你们要白白地劳力；因为你们的地不出土产，其上的树木也不结果子。
verses.en: Your strength will be used up in vain; your land will not give its yield, and the trees of the land[NOTE:1] will not produce their fruit.
notes: Heb “the tree of the land will not give its fruit.” The collective singular has been translated as a plural. One Hebrew ms from Cairo Geniza, other medieval Hebrew mss, Smr, LXX, and Tg. Ps.-J. have “the field” as in v. 4, rather than “the land.”

verses.zh: 「你们行事若与我反对，不肯听从我，我就要按你们的罪加七倍降灾与你们。
verses.en: “‘If you walk in hostility against me[NOTE:1] and are not willing to obey me, I will increase your affliction[NOTE:2] seven times according to your sins.
notes: Heb “hostile with me,” but see the added preposition ב (bet) on the phrase “in hostility” in v. 24 and 27.
Heb “your blow, stroke”; cf. TEV “punishment”; NLT “I will inflict you with seven more disasters.”

verses.zh: 我也要打发野地的走兽到你们中间，抢吃你们的儿女，吞灭你们的牲畜，使你们的人数减少，道路荒凉。
verses.en: I will send the wild animals[NOTE:1] against you, and they will bereave you of your children,[NOTE:2] annihilate your cattle, and diminish your population[NOTE:3] so that your roads will become deserted.
notes: Heb “the animal of the field.” This collective singular has been translated as a plural. The expression “animal of the field” refers to a wild (i.e., nondomesticated) animal.
The words “of your children” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.
Heb “and diminish you.”

verses.zh: 「你们因这些事若仍不改正归我，行事与我反对，
verses.en: “‘If in spite of these things[NOTE:1] you do not allow yourselves to be disciplined and you walk in hostility against me,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And if in these.”
Heb “with me,” but see the added preposition ב (bet) on the phrase “in hostility” in vv. 24 and 27.

verses.zh: 我就要行事与你们反对，因你们的罪击打你们七次。
verses.en: then I myself will also walk in hostility against you and strike you[NOTE:1] seven times on account of your sins.
notes: Heb “and I myself will also strike you.”

verses.zh: 我又要使刀剑临到你们，报复你们背约的仇；聚集你们在各城内，降瘟疫在你们中间，也必将你们交在仇敌的手中。
verses.en: I will bring on you an avenging sword, a covenant vengeance.[NOTE:1] Although[NOTE:2] you will gather together into your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be given into enemy hands.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “vengeance of covenant”; cf. NAB “the avenger of my covenant.”
Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) has a concessive force in this context.
Heb “in hand of enemy,” but Tg. Ps.-J. and Tg. Neof. have “in the hands of your enemies” (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 454).

verses.zh: 我要折断你们的杖，就是断绝你们的粮。那时，必有十个女人在一个炉子给你们烤饼，按分量秤给你们；你们要吃，也吃不饱。
verses.en: When I break off your supply of bread,[NOTE:1] ten women will bake your bread in one oven; they will ration your bread by weight,[NOTE:2] and you will eat and not be satisfied.
notes: Heb “When I break to you staff of bread” (KJV, ASV, and NASB all similar).
Heb “they will return your bread in weight.”

verses.zh: 「你们因这一切的事若不听从我，却行事与我反对，
verses.en: “‘If in spite of this[NOTE:1] you do not obey me but walk in hostility against me,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And if in this.”
Heb “with me.”

verses.zh: 我就要发烈怒，行事与你们反对，又因你们的罪惩罚你们七次。
verses.en: I will walk in hostile rage against you,[NOTE:1] and I myself will also discipline you seven times on account of your sins.
notes: Heb “in rage of hostility with you”; NASB “with wrathful hostility”; NRSV “I will continue hostile to you in fury”; CEV “I’ll get really furious.”

verses.zh: 并且你们要吃儿子的肉，也要吃女儿的肉。
verses.en: You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.” The phrase “you will eat” has not been repeated in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 我又要毁坏你们的邱坛，砍下你们的日像，把你们的尸首扔在你们偶像的身上；我的心也必厌恶你们。
verses.en: I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars,[NOTE:1] and I will stack your dead bodies on top of the lifeless bodies of your idols.[NOTE:2] I will abhor you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Regarding these cultic installations, see the remarks in B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 188, and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:903. The term rendered “incense altars” might better be rendered “sanctuaries [of foreign deities]” or “stelae.”

The translation reflects the Hebrew wordplay “your corpses…the corpses of your idols.” Since idols, being lifeless, do not really have “corpses,” the translation uses “dead bodies” for people and “lifeless bodies” for the idols.
Heb “and my soul will abhor you.”

verses.zh: 我要使你们的城邑变为荒凉，使你们的众圣所成为荒场；我也不闻你们馨香的香气。
verses.en: I will lay your cities waste[NOTE:1] and make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will refuse to smell your soothing aromas.
notes: Heb “And I will give your cities a waste”; NLT “make your cities desolate.”

verses.zh: 我要使地成为荒场，住在其上的仇敌就因此诧异。
verses.en: I myself will make the land desolate, and your enemies who live in it will be appalled.

verses.zh: 我要把你们散在列邦中；我也要拔刀追赶你们。你们的地要成为荒场；你们的城邑要变为荒凉。
verses.en: I will scatter you among the nations and unsheathe the sword[NOTE:1] after you, so your land will become desolate and your cities will become a waste.
notes: Heb “and I will empty sword” (see HALOT 1228 s.v. ריק 3).

verses.zh: 「你们在仇敌之地居住的时候，你们的地荒凉，要享受众安息；正在那时候，地要歇息，享受安息。
verses.en: “‘Then the land will make up for[NOTE:1] its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and make up its Sabbaths.
notes: There are two Hebrew roots רָצָה (ratsah), one meaning “to be pleased with; to take pleasure” (HALOT 1280-81 s.v. רצה; cf. “enjoy” in NASB, NIV, NRSV, and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 452), and the other meaning “to restore” (HALOT 1281-82 s.v. II רצה; cf. NAB “retrieve” and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 189).

verses.zh: 地多时为荒场，就要多时歇息；地这样歇息，是你们住在其上的安息年所不能得的。
verses.en: All the days of the desolation it will have the rest it did not have[NOTE:1] on your Sabbaths when you lived on it.
notes: Heb “it shall rest which it did not rest.”

verses.zh: 至于你们剩下的人，我要使他们在仇敌之地心惊胆怯。叶子被风吹的响声，要追赶他们；他们要逃避，像人逃避刀剑，无人追赶，却要跌倒。
verses.en: “‘As for[NOTE:1] the ones who remain among you, I will bring despair into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a blowing leaf will pursue them, and they will flee as one who flees the sword and will fall down even though there is no pursuer.
notes: Heb “And.”

verses.zh: 无人追赶，他们要彼此撞跌，像在刀剑之前。你们在仇敌面前也必站立不住。
verses.en: They will stumble over each other as those who flee before a sword, though[NOTE:1] there is no pursuer, and there will be no one to take a stand[NOTE:2] for you before your enemies.
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) is used in a concessive sense here.
The term rendered “to stand up” is a noun, not an infinitive. It occurs only here and appears to designate someone who would take a powerful stand for them against their enemies.

verses.zh: 你们要在列邦中灭亡；仇敌之地要吞吃你们。
verses.en: You will perish among the nations; the land of your enemies will consume you.

verses.zh: 你们剩下的人必因自己的罪孽和祖宗的罪孽在仇敌之地消灭。
verses.en: “‘As for the ones who remain among you, they will rot away because of[NOTE:1] their iniquity in the lands of your enemies, and they will also rot away because of their ancestors’[NOTE:2] iniquities which are with them.
notes: Heb “in” (so KJV, ASV; also later in this verse).
Heb “fathers’” (also in the following verse).

verses.zh: 「他们要承认自己的罪和他们祖宗的罪，就是干犯我的那罪，并且承认自己行事与我反对，
verses.en: However, when[NOTE:1] they confess their iniquity and their ancestors’ iniquities which they committed by trespassing against me,[NOTE:2] by which they also walked[NOTE:3] in hostility against me[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “And.” Many English versions take this to be a conditional clause (“if…”) though there is no conditional particle (see, e.g., NASB, NIV, NRSV; but see the very different rendering in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 190). The temporal translation offered here (“when”) takes into account the particle אָז (ʾaz, “then”), which occurs twice in v. 41. The obvious contextual contrast between vv. 39 and 40 is expressed by “however” in the translation.
Heb “in their trespassing which they trespassed in me.” See the note on Lev 5:15, although the term is used in a more technical sense there in relation to the “guilt offering.”
Heb “and also which they walked.”
Heb “with me.”

verses.zh: 我所以行事与他们反对，把他们带到仇敌之地。那时，他们未受割礼的心若谦卑了，他们也服了罪孽的刑罚，
verses.en: (and I myself will walk in hostility against them and bring them into the land of their enemies), and[NOTE:1] then their uncircumcised hearts become humbled and they make up for[NOTE:2] their iniquities,
notes: Heb “or then,” although the LXX has “then” and the Syriac “and then.”
Heb “and then they make up for.” On the verb “make up for” see the note on v. 34 above.

verses.zh: 我就要记念我与雅各所立的约，与以撒所立的约，与亚伯拉罕所立的约，并要记念这地。
verses.en: I will remember my covenant with Jacob and also my covenant with Isaac and also my covenant with Abraham,[NOTE:1] and I will remember the land.
notes: Heb “my covenant with Abraham I will remember.” The phrase “I will remember” has not been repeated in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 他们离开这地，地在荒废无人的时候就要享受安息。并且他们要服罪孽的刑罚；因为他们厌弃了我的典章，心中厌恶了我的律例。
verses.en: The land will be abandoned by them[NOTE:1] in order that it may make up for[NOTE:2] its Sabbaths while it is made desolate[NOTE:3] without them,[NOTE:4] and they will make up for their iniquity because[NOTE:5] they have rejected my regulations and have abhorred[NOTE:6] my statutes.
notes: Heb “from them.” The preposition “from” refers here to the agent of the action (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 455).
The jussive form of the verb with the simple vav (ו) here calls for a translation that expresses purpose.
The verb is the Hophal infinitive construct with the third feminine singular suffix (GKC 182 §67.y; cf. v. 34).
Heb “from them.”
Heb “because and in because,” a double expression, which is used only here and in Ezek 13:10 (without the vav) for emphasis (GKC 492 §158.b).
Heb “and their soul has abhorred.”

verses.zh: 虽是这样，他们在仇敌之地，我却不厌弃他们，也不厌恶他们，将他们尽行灭绝，也不背弃我与他们所立的约，因为我是耶和华―他们的　神。
verses.en: In spite of this, however, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them and abhor them to make a complete end of them, to break my covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.

verses.zh: 我却要为他们的缘故记念我与他们先祖所立的约。他们的先祖是我在列邦人眼前、从埃及地领出来的，为要作他们的　神。我是耶和华。」
verses.en: I will remember for them the covenant with their ancestors[NOTE:1] whom I brought out from the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “covenant of former ones.” sn For similar expressions referring back to the ancestors who refused to follow the stipulations of the Mosaic covenant see, for example, Deut 19:14, Jer 11:10, and Ps 79:8 (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 192, and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 471).

verses.zh: 这些律例、典章，和法度是耶和华与以色列人在西奈山藉着摩西立的。
verses.en: These are the statutes, regulations, and instructions which the Lord established[NOTE:1] between himself and the Israelites at Mount Sinai through[NOTE:2] Moses.
notes: Heb “gave” (so NLT); KJV, ASV, NCV “made.”
Heb “by the hand of” (so KJV).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must
not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

BACKGROUND STUDY

- Leviticus 26 seems to reflect the structure of Hittite Suzerain treaties of the second millennium B.C. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN)
TREATIES. The same type of pattern can be seen in the book of Deuteronomy and Joshua 24. The outline of chapter
26 is as follows:

- the blessings, Lev. 26:1-13

- the cursings, Lev. 26:14-39

- the possibility of restitution, Lev. 26:40-46

Blessings and curses connected to law codes were common in the second millennium B.C., but not in the first millennium
B.C. This is evidence for the historicity of Moses' authorship. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH.

- The "blessing" and "cursing" pattern is also repeated in Deuteronomy 27-28. Remember, the Mosaic Covenant is a
conditional covenant (cf. Exod. 19:5-6; 23:22; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT). Blessing follows obedience (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP). However,
disobedience brings judgment. Actions have consequences in time and eternity (i.e., the Two Ways of Wisdom Literature,
cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1; Gal. 6:7).

- For an ANE historical perspective on treaty conditions, see D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks,
chapter 4, "How Does the Language of Destruction and Blessing Work?" pp. 73-128.

- Chapter 26 seems to conclude the book of Leviticus, while chapter 27 is a miscellaneous appendix on vows.

26:1 "idols" This verse lists four kinds of idolatry.

- idols (BDB 47, cf. Lev. 19:4)

- image (BDB 820, cf. Exod. 20:4)

- sacred pillar (BDB 663, cf. Exod. 23:24; 34:13)

- figured stones (BDB 67 CONSTRUCT BDB 967, found only here; see PLURAL in Num. 33:52)

The very fact that all of these different types of idolatry are mentioned shows that Israel had been affected
by her neighbors even at this early stage. This chapter reflects part of the Ten Commandments (cf. Exod. 20:3-6). They
must worship YHWH alone!

▣ "I am the Lord your God" This is covenant language, found so often in the
Pentateuch. It has the two most common names for Israel's Deity.

- Lord = YHWH, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D

- God = Elohim, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C

In this chapter it is repeated in vv. 1, 2, 13, 44, 45.

26:2 "keep My sabbaths and reverence My sanctuary" This relates to Exod. 20:7-11. Taking God's name in
vain involved worship at the sanctuary. The VERB "keep" is IMPERFECT but used in
an IMPERATIVE sense. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP.

26:3 "if. . ." This section shows the conditional and unconditional elements of every Old Testament covenant.
God always comes to man with unconditional promises but man is expected to respond in covenant terms
(cf. Deuteronomy 27; 28; Joshua 8; 24). It is interesting that the "if. . .then" section of vv. 1-13 is followed by "if you do not. . ."
in vv. 14ff. See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "statutes. . .commandments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR
GOD'S REVELATION.

26:4-13 This is the "blessing" component of the Mosaic Covenant.

- rain in its season for abundant crops, Lev. 26:4-5,10; Deut. 28:12

- security in your land, Lev. 26:5-6

- invaders, Lev. 26:7-8

- wild beasts

- health and growth of the people, Lev. 26:9

- security with YHWH's presence, Lev. 26:11-13

- YHWH will dwell with them, Lev. 26:11a

- YHWH will not reject them, Lev. 26:11b

- YHWH will walk among them, Lev. 26:12

- YHWH's past acts reveal

- His character is gracious

- His power is unstoppable

- His promises are sure

26:4 "I will give you rains in their seasons" YHWH was always the giver of agricultural blessings but somehow the
Israelis began worshiping Ba'al as the source of fertility. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE.

26:5 This verse is imagery to express an abundant crop. Before one harvest time is finished another will start.

26:6 "peace" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom).

26:8 "five" This is not normally a symbolic number. See NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 190-191.

26:9 "I will confirm My covenant with you" The VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil
PERFECT with waw) basically means "to arise," "to stand up," but in the Hiphil it takes
on the meaning "to establish" or "to ratify" (cf. Gen. 6:18; 9:9,11; 17:19,21; Exod. 6:4; Ezek. 16:62).

26:11 "I will make My dwelling among you. . .I will also walk among you" The greatest promise that God can give
is His presence (cf. Exod. 25:8). This was symbolically represented by the Tabernacle and particularly the ark of the covenant.
See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT.

The uncial MS B and the LXX have "covenant" instead of "tabernacle with" or "dwelling place."

- YHWH's rejection of His people, Lev. 26:11,30,44

- Israel's rejection of Him, Lev. 26:15,43

The Hebrew root can denote (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 883):

- consider something or someone as "dung"

- consider something or someone as "spoiled food"; the same imagery (i.e., different root, BDB 596, KB 628) is

26:12 "I will walk among you" This is literally "walk to and fro" (BDB 229, KB 246, Hithpael
PERFECT with waw).

This idiom is also found in this same form in Gen. 3:8, for God's presence in the Garden of Eden with
Adam and Eve before the fall.

The VERB "walk" is also found in the Qal stem several times (Lev. 26:3, 21,
23, 24, 27, 28, 40, 41).

- "walk" as lifestyle obedience, Lev. 26:3 (used of the Patriarch's walk of faith in Gen. 5:22,24; 6:9; 17:1; 24:40; 48:15)

- "walk" as imagery of YHWH's presence (i.e., Gen. 3:8), Lev. 26:12 (cf. Deut. 23:4)

- act with hostility toward YHWH, Lev. 26:21, 23, 24, 27, 28, 40, 41

▣ "and be your God, and you shall be My people" This is covenant terminology (cf. Gen. 17:7; 26:24;
Exod. 6:7; Jer. 7:23; 11:4). Israel was YHWH's special people (cf. Exod. 19:5-6; 1 Kgs. 8:51-53).

26:13 "who brought you out of the land of Egypt" This is a regular part of Hittite Suzerain treaties where
the historical acts were given of the king who was making the covenant. The exodus was God's great act of grace
to the Hebrew people (cf. Gen. 15:12-22). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES.

▣ "made you walk erect" This is an idiom for slaves walking with heads up, as free people. No longer
are they bent over under the yoke of slavery.

23"'And if by these things you are not turned to Me, but act with hostility against Me, 24then I will

26:23 This verse clearly shows that the purpose of YHWH's judgments is restoration. YHWH desires a
people who reflect His character to a pagan world.

26:25-26 In the OT there are three things that YHWH sends as judgment (i.e., 1 Chr. 21:11-12; 2 Chr. 20:9).

- the sword (i.e., warfare, invasion)

- pestilence (i.e., disease normally from a siege)

- famine (no stored foodstuffs, nor growing crops, cf. Ps. 105:16)

Often the "wild beasts" are mentioned as returning!

26:26 "staff of bread" In the OT, this Hebrew NOUN (BDB 641), which means a part of a tree
from which a staff, rod, or scepter is made, has several meanings.

- a way of referring to a tribe

- Moses' shepherd staff or rod, which was a symbol of YHWH's power

- Aaron's tribal banner pole

- a metaphor for that which the outstretched arm gives; here it refers to bread rations (cf. Ps. 105:16; Ezek. 4:16; 5:16; 14:13)

- scepter (cf. Ezek. 19:11)

- wooden carrier of bread (NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 38)

26:29 "you will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters" This refers to siege warfare
where cannibalism and disease were rampant (cf. 2 Kgs. 6:28-29; Lam. 2:20).

26:30 "high places" This is the characteristic place of Ba'al worship (cf. Hos. 4:11-14; Jer. 3:6-10).
Connected with the uplifted stone, which was the symbol of Ba'al, was also either a live, planted tree or a
carved stake which was a symbol of Ashtoreth (cf. Deut. 7:5; 12:3; 16:21). We also learn from this chapter
about the incense altars which were connected with the Ba'al altars (cf. 2 Chr. 34:4,7). See

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP IN THE ANE.

▣ "My soul shall abhor you" This chapter must be viewed in anthropomorphic terms. The author is
attributing human emotions to Deity. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE DEITY.

Notice the number of "I's" in this chapter (similar to Ezek. 36:22-36).

26:31 "I will not smell your soothing aromas" This is a metaphor of God receiving their sacrifices. As
the smoke from the altar arose it went symbolically before God. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: A SOOTHING AROMA.

26:32-33 This is a specific reference to the exile, which would occur if they practiced the same abomination
as the Canaanites did (cf. Gen. 15:12-22). We know from history that this is exactly what happened to the northern ten
tribes by Assyria in 722 B.C. and to Judah by Babylon in 586 B.C.

26:32 One VERB (BDB 1030, KB 1663) is used in two senses.

- Hiphil = "be desolate"

- Qal = "be appalled"

26:41 "if their uncircumcised heart" Circumcision became a symbol for that which is dedicated to God,
therefore, in the Old Testament, there is the uncircumcised heart (cf. Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4), lip (cf. Exod. 6:12,20),
and ear (cf. Jer. 6:10). Here, it became a metaphor for humbleness and openness toward God (i.e., 2 Chr. 7:14).

26:42 "I will remember My covenant with Jacob" Here we have an affirmation of God going back to His
original covenant with Abraham in Genesis 12 (cf. Lev. 26:45). It was the original covenant whose
stipulations guided God's dealing with the people of God. When God speaks His words can be trusted. His
promises are unconditional (i.e., His redemption plan for all humans), but they are conditional on every
individual and generation responding to them appropriately. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO PATRIARCHS.

26:45 "in the sight of the nations" It must be remembered that Israel was to be a kingdom of priests to bring all of the
world to God (cf. Exod. 19:4-5). The people of the world knew of God from Israel but the problem was that when Israel sinned,
God was revealed only in judgment and not in love and blessing. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How does Lev. 26:1 reflect Exodus 20?

- Why was Israel's idolatry so theologically significant?

- Explain the significance of the four "My's" in Lev. 26:2-3.

- How is Leviticus 26 related to Hittite treaties? How does this help us date Moses' writings?

- Explain the theological significance of the VERB in Lev. 26:11a.

- Explain why the "if's" in this chapter are so significant.

- Can humans break YHWH's covenant? (Lev. 26:15)

- Explain the idiom "My face" in Lev. 26:17.

- Do the prophets use the material in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28?

- What does "the land will enjoy its sabbaths" mean? (Lev. 26:34)

- To whom does Lev. 26:36 refer?

- Why is Lev. 26:40-45 so theologically significant?

- How does Lev. 26:42 relate to Genesis?
